Lessons.Title: Ways to Find Unknown Length (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use the attributes of two-dimensional figures (such as perimeter and symmetry) to reason about side lengths.
In the previous lesson, you used given side lengths and symmetry to find the perimeter of a figure. In this lesson, you reason in the other direction—given the perimeter and information about symmetry, you find the side lengths of two-dimensional figures. You also practice completing a figure given a line of symmetry and half of the figure, and then reason about the perimeter of the whole figure.

2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up: True or False: Equations with Fractions (10 minutes); Activity 1: Unknown Lengths (20 minutes); Activity 2: Lin’s Design (15 minutes); Cool-down: Stage Symmetry (5 minutes)
Source-goal geometric reasoning: To find unknown lengths from perimeter, subtract the total known side lengths, then use the figure's equal-side or symmetry constraints.

Edulytics worked explanation: Use the original 64-inch-perimeter diagrams; identify matching sides first. For a rectangle of perimeter 64 inches and one side 12 inches, double the known side then subtract: 64 − 24 = 40. Divide 40 across the other two equal sides to obtain 20 inches each.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (not gated original): A rectangle has perimeter 64 inches and one side 14 inches. Find the other side.
Original student diagrams, teacher card sorting, paper folding, and physical drawings require figure-by-figure / teacher validation.
